tool_input.description: Temporarily restore buggy controller and run new tests

result:
The fix is in place and verified.

`app/Http/Controllers/ProfileController.ts` was reading the request body raw (`this.request.json<ProfileInput>()`) and spreading it into `User.forceUpdate`, which both skipped all validation and bypassed the model's mass-assignment protection — so an unparsed `id` or `passwordHash` from the payload was written straight to the row. `update()` now parses the body with `this.validateBody(ProfileUpdateSchema)` (the already-present `app/Http/Validators/ProfileValidator.ts`, which mirrors the registration rules: required name trimmed to ≤120 chars, required well-formed lowercase email, optional password of ≥8 characters where empty means "keep current"), so invalid input raises a `ValidationException` → 422 with per-field `name`/`email`/`password` errors the profile page already renders, before anything touches the database; the write then uses `User.update` with only the validated `name`, `email`, and optional `password`, so fields outside the form are ignored and the `password` → `passwordHash` hashing still goes through `AuthenticatableModel`'s fillable path. I also added `tests/ProfileController.test.ts`, covering rejection of a malformed email and of an empty name (asserting the stored row is unchanged) plus a valid update that carries extra `id`/`passwordHash` fields, asserting those are ignored while name and lowercased email are saved; the tests fail against the pre-fix controller and are safe to rerun against the persistent test database. `bun run typecheck` and `bun test` (5 tests) both pass.
